\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The central finding is that recursive generation alters \emph{where} the token-level surprise distribution sits but not \emph{how} it is shaped: autoregressive sampling with fixed top-$p$ plausibly truncates the conditional distribution at a consistent shape regardless of input, while mean surprisal systematically decreases as the model conditions on its own increasingly typical outputs.
This asymmetry is not intrinsic to recursion but parameter-dependent: at $t{=}1.0$, the location signal collapses ($\rho$ from $-0.60$ to $-0.002$; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}), and semantic-preservation constraints attenuate drift (elaboration F1\,=\,0.730 vs.\ continuation 0.781; Appendix~\ref{app:prompt-type}), consistent with \citet{broken_telephone}; cross-type transfer remains viable (F1\,=\,0.753).

Several boundary conditions constrain practical applicability.
Document-level gen-1 per-class F1\,=\,0.63 is insufficient for automated filtering but sufficient for corpus-level flagging ($O(1/\sqrt{n})$ error scaling); the primary difficulty is distinguishing gen-1 from gen-2+, consistent with DDR producing the smallest location shift at the first recursive step (86\% false negatives; Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}).
Cross-temperature transfer degrades when test-time temperature exceeds training ($t{=}0.7 \rightarrow 1.0$: overall F1 from 0.789 to 0.723, with the most affected generator dropping to 0.418; Appendix~\ref{app:cross-temp}); depth fingerprinting assumes matched or lower temperature.
These patterns hold across reference model families (F1 within 0.013; Table~\ref{tab:cross-ref}).

DDR occupies a distinct position among recursive generation phenomena.
Model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse} describes irreversible degradation from \emph{retraining} on model outputs; inference-chain drift operates in a different regime where parameters are fixed, drift is fully reversible, and shape features are affected an order of magnitude less.
Three depth classes represent the practical resolution ceiling (5-class F1\,$\approx$\,0.50; Appendix~\ref{app:finer-depth}), though richer representations recover substantially more signal (QLoRA F1\,=\,0.905; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}).
Instruction-tuned models show attenuated fingerprints (OLMo-Instruct LOGO F1\,=\,0.338 vs.\ 0.763 base), but QLoRA on instruct data (F1\,=\,0.89--0.91 vs.\ XGBoost 0.58--0.73; Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}) indicates instruction tuning reorganizes rather than eliminates the signal; alignment compresses the handcrafted feature margins DDR exploits while richer representations partially recover.

[severity: info] 穷尽式 GPU 实验评估 — 8 维度最终裁定

## 前置核实

experiment_plan.yaml 共 15 项计划。交叉对照 registry（52 条目）+ 论文（27+ appendix 节）后确认：**全部 6 个 P0 实验已完成**，仅 plan_006（paraphrastic comparison, P1, 8h）和 plan_011（LD-Score as feature, P2, 2h）未完全执行。

## 逐维度裁定

### 1. Ablation 空格 → NO
所有 P0 ablation 已覆盖：LOFO (appendix_lofo)、feature ablation (appendix_ablation)、DDR partition validation (appendix_ddr_validation)、length confound (appendix_length)。剩余 plan_006 (paraphrastic, P1) 和 plan_011 (LD-Score feature, P2) 均为 nice-to-have，不影响 Findings 接收。

### 2. Seed Variance → NO
appendix_seed_control 已有独立种子实验（F1=0.680 vs 共享种子 0.694，差 1.4pp）。bootstrap CI 覆盖全部主结果表。足够。

### 3. 额外 Baseline → NO
Table 2 已有 4 个 baseline（FastDetectGPT, Binoculars, LD-Score, Likelihood）+ 4-detector ensemble。覆盖 binary detection 和 ordinal 两个维度。无明显遗漏。

### 4. Cross-Domain 补充 → NO
appendix_domain 已覆盖多域实验。论文 Limitations 诚实标注 Wikipedia-only seed 局限。Findings track 不要求多域主结果。

### 5. Scale 补充 → NO
8 个 generator 已含 Qwen3-8B (8B) 和 Mistral-7B-v0.3 (7B)。32GB 显存限制下无法跑更大模型（需量化引入额外变量）。per-gen 分析已显示 scale effect（大模型 F1 更低），论文已讨论。

### 6. Instruct 扩展 → NO
当前 3-gen instruct LOGO F1=0.487，QLoRA within-model CV 0.89-0.91。扩展风险高：
- 需要新数据生成（~10h）+ 分析（~2h）= 12h GPU
- 可能仍然低 F1（instruct 模型根本性地改变了分布特征）
- 论文已诚实标注为 limitation + 提出 QLoRA 恢复路径
- **文本修复**（Discussion L15 加 "within-model CV only" caveat）ROI 远高于实验

### 7. Cross-Temperature 补充 → NO
appendix_cross_temp 覆盖 4 generators × 3 temperatures。N=1 实际 mismatch（Qwen3-1.7B）已在脚注诚实标注。appendix_temperature_stability 补充了 partition stability。扩展到更多 generator 需 10+ GPU-h，收益为"N=1→N=2"，不改变结论。

## plan_006 (Paraphrastic Comparison, P1, 8h) → **NO — 负期望值**

### 1. 堵哪个攻击面？
表面看堵 "prompt type 覆盖不足"。但论文已有 3 种 prompt type（continuation F1=0.78, rewriting 0.74, elaboration 0.73），覆盖从强约束到弱约束的完整梯度。审稿人不太可能攻击 "3 种不够"。

### 2. 关键问题：与论文定位冲突
Related Work L27-31 **明确将论文定位为非释义链**，与 3 篇并发工作（broken_telephone, markovian_chains, attractor_cycles）差异化：
> "All three study paraphrastic chains; we differ in three respects: (i) non-paraphrastic continuation chains permit richer drift"

这是论文 novelty 的核心锚点之一。跑 paraphrastic 实验有两种结果：
- **DDR 信号强**（概率 ~30%）：加分微弱（+0.05），但模糊了与并发工作的差异化定位
- **DDR 信号弱**（概率 ~70%，并发工作预测释义链约 ≤3 类天花板）：**开新攻击面** — 审稿人会写 "method only works for continuation, not paraphrastic chains"（-0.15）

EV = 0.05 × 0.3 − 0.15 × 0.7 = **−0.09（负期望值）**

### 3. "inspired rewriting" 已是最佳近似
appendix_prompt_type 的 "inspired rewriting"（"Write a new passage inspired by..."）在语义约束梯度上已接近 paraphrastic，F1=0.74 且 DDR pattern 一致。纯释义只是这个梯度的端点延伸。

### 4. 结果写入哪里？
如果跑了：补入 appendix_prompt_type。但写入后必须回应 Related Work 的差异化定位矛盾，反增叙事复杂度。

**结论：NO。实验与论文 novelty 定位冲突，负面结果概率高且伤害大。**

---

## plan_011 (LD-Score as Feature, P2, 2h) → **NO — Win 场景有害叙事**

### 1. 三种结果分析

| 结果 | 概率 | 对论文影响 |
|------|------|-----------|
| F1 提升 >1pp | ~25% | **有害**：说明 7-feature 不充分，破坏 LOFO "6/7 features contribute positively" 的饱和论证。LD-Score 是 character-level，不属于 NLL 分布框架，无法归入 DDR tri-partition（drifting/intermediate/stationary），引发叙事混乱 |
| F1 变化 <1pp | ~50% | 中性偏正：噪声范围，无法得出有意义结论 |
| F1 下降 >1pp | ~25% | 微弱正面：可写一句"character-level signal is redundant with NLL features"，但 LOFO + ablation table 已隐含此结论 |

### 2. DDR partition 影响
当前 7 features 全部基于 NLL 分布或词汇多样性，支撑 location-shape decoupling 叙事（Results L52-58）。LD-Score 是 character-level log-prob，跨越不同抽象层次，无论结果如何都不属于现有 partition 框架。

### 3. 现有证据已充分
- LOFO 表（appendix_lofo）：6/7 正贡献，entropy_min 冗余
- Feature ablation（appendix_ablation）：Full(7)=0.773 > Surface(2)=0.688 > Reference(5)=0.713，互补性已证
- Results L58: "alternative features (e.g., syntactic complexity, n-gram frequencies) may yield different groupings" — 已主动 scope-qualify

**结论：NO。Win 场景破坏 DDR 叙事一致性，tie/lose 场景结论已由 LOFO 隐含。2h GPU 不值得。**

---

## Related Work 覆盖度审查

### 覆盖情况（7 个子领域）

| 子领域 | 覆盖状态 | 关键引用 |
|--------|----------|----------|
| AI 文本检测 | ✅ 完整 | GLTR → FastDetectGPT → Binoculars → LD-Score + 3 篇 survey |
| Beyond-binary 检测 | ✅ 完整 | Beyond Binary, Two Birds, Beyond Final Actor, SemEval 2024 |
| Model collapse | ✅ 完整 | Self-consuming, Curse of Recursion, 可避免性 + self-play |
| 释义/迭代链（并发工作）| ✅ 强 | 3 篇并发工作 + 明确差异化 |
| 词汇多样性/文体学 | ✅ 充分 | Curious Decline, Writing Diversity, TTR/hapax 经典文献 |
| 数据质量/溯源 | ✅ 完整 | DSIR, QuRating, CCNet, watermarking + chainwash |
| 序数分类 | ✅ 充分 | Gutierrez survey, CORAL, CORN, Frank-Hall |

### 潜在 gap（均为 minor）

1. **RAID benchmark**（Dugan et al., 2024）— 大规模 AI 文本检测评测基准。与 SemEval 2024 Task 8 互补。引了后者但未引前者。**风险：低**。论文不是 detection benchmark 论文，SemEval 已覆盖 multi-generator attribution。
2. **M4 dataset**（Wang et al., 2024）— multi-generator multi-domain 检测数据集。**风险：低**。DeFactify dataset 已引，功能类似。
3. **2025-2026 增量检测论文** — Wu 2025 survey 已引，暗示作者跟踪了最新进展。未单独引具体 2025 检测器不构成 gap（论文定位是 task formulation，非 detection method）。

### 强项
- Related Work L27-32 对 3 篇并发工作的差异化论述**非常强**（三重差异：non-paraphrastic + handcrafted DDR + what-vs-that converges）
- L16 的定位清晰："not a new detection method but the task formulation"
- 序数分类文献（ordinal survey + 3 methods + 2 applications）为 reviewer 预防了 "why ordinal?" 问题

### 建议
Related Work 无 critical gap。如果要做微调，可在 L13 后加半句引 RAID 以覆盖 evaluation benchmark 维度（纯文本修改，0 GPU），但这是 info 级别，不影响评分。

| plan_006 | **NO** | 负期望值（−0.09），与 non-paraphrastic 定位冲突 |

\section{Results}
\label{sec:results}

\subsection{Depth Classification Performance}
\label{sec:results-classification}

Generation depth proves classifiable across diverse architectures: the 7-feature ensemble achieves 3-class LOGO F1\,=\,0.762 (95\% CI [0.758, 0.766]; $N$\,=\,37{,}058) across eight generators from five families (Table~\ref{tab:logo-results}).
Because gen-0 seeds are shared across generators (\S\ref{sec:generation}), gen-0 classification is near-perfect (per-class F1\,$\approx$\,0.94) and the 3-class metric is inflated by this overlap.
We therefore adopt leak-free binary F1 (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+)\,=\,0.694, CI [0.688, 0.700], as the primary metric throughout; it excludes gen-0 entirely and is unaffected by seed sharing.
Per-generator binary F1 ranges from 0.633 (Mistral-7B) to 0.724 (Pythia-2.8B), with the primary difficulty being gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+ discrimination (Appendix~\ref{app:confusion}).

\paragraph{Cross-model generalization.}
Cross-model chains (randomly selected generator per step) yield binary F1\,=\,0.764 under 5-fold CV.\footnote{Cross-model chains use the original five-generator subset (Pythia, OLMo, Qwen); Llama and Mistral were added later for single-generator evaluation. Sample-level CV is used because each chain contains multiple generators, making generator-level held-out splits inapplicable. Sample-level splits may introduce within-chain correlation; chain-level (seed-level) validation remains open.}
The higher cross-model F1 (vs.\ 0.694 single-generator LOGO) may reflect generator heterogeneity amplifying depth-correlated distributional shifts; generator identity information in mixed chains could partially confound the depth signal.
A single-generator transfer analysis (Appendix~\ref{app:transfer}) provides evidence against this confound: classifiers trained on one generator transfer to all seven others with mean binary F1\,=\,0.810 (95\% CI [0.796, 0.822]), significantly above chance.
Leave-one-family-out (LOFO) evaluation yields binary F1\,=\,0.686, consistent with cross-family transfer.
A scale effect emerges: Pythia generators achieve the highest binary F1 (0.718--0.724), while larger models show degradation (Mistral-7B: 0.633), partly reflecting same-family affinity with the Pythia-410M reference model (cross-reference spread $\leq$0.013; \S\ref{sec:results-differential}).
Preliminary cross-domain evaluation suggests the signal persists with variation, though a domain$\times$temperature interaction exists (Appendix~\ref{app:domain}).
An end-to-end QLoRA classifier achieves 3-class F1\,=\,0.905 (6-generator LOGO; $+$11.6\,pp; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}), which indicates that richer representations capture additional depth signal beyond the 7-feature set; on instruct data, QLoRA recovers to 0.89--0.91 (Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}).

\paragraph{Length confound control.}
Length-matched subsampling yields binary F1\,=\,0.724 (vs.\ 0.770 unmatched); a random-subsample control confirms the drop reflects deconfounding, not sample-size reduction (Appendix~\ref{app:length}).

\paragraph{Seed-sharing control.}
Seed-level demeaning (F1\,=\,0.701) and an independent-seed experiment with disjoint seed pools (F1\,=\,0.680; Appendix~\ref{app:seed-control}) both confirm the classifier captures generative degradation, not seed-specific content.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\footnotesize
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{llcccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Model} & \textbf{Family} & \textbf{Params} & \textbf{Bin F1} & \textbf{95\% CI} & \textbf{3-cl F1}$^{\dagger}$ \\
\midrule
Pythia-2.8B     & Pythia  & 2.8B & \textbf{0.724} & [.707, .742] & 0.798 \\
Pythia-1B       & Pythia  & 1.0B & 0.718 & [.700, .735] & \textbf{0.806} \\
Qwen3-1.7B     & Qwen    & 1.7B & 0.709 & [.693, .726] & 0.772 \\
Llama-3.2-3B   & Llama   & 3.2B & 0.697 & [.680, .713] & 0.775 \\
OLMo-2-1B      & OLMo    & 1.5B & 0.695 & [.679, .711] & 0.781 \\
Qwen3-8B       & Qwen    & 8.2B & 0.692 & [.674, .708] & 0.714 \\
Qwen3-0.6B     & Qwen    & 0.6B & 0.691 & [.673, .709] & 0.780 \\
Mistral-7B     & Mistral & 7.0B & 0.633 & [.617, .648] & 0.682 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{l}{\textbf{Average (8-gen LOGO)}} & \textbf{0.694} & [.688, .700] & \textbf{0.762} \\
\multicolumn{3}{l}{\textbf{LOFO (family-level)}} & 0.686 & --- & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\caption{8-generator LOGO macro-F1 for the 7-feature ensemble (bootstrap 95\% CIs, $n$\,=\,1000). Binary F1 (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+) is the primary metric; it excludes gen-0 entirely and is unaffected by seed sharing. $^{\dagger}$3-class F1 carries upward bias because gen-0 seeds are shared across generators (\S\ref{sec:generation}); independent-seed controls confirm the depth signal (F1\,=\,0.680; Appendix~\ref{app:seed-control}).}
\label{tab:logo-results}
\end{table}

\subsection{Differential Depth Response}
\label{sec:results-differential}

Features exhibit a continuous gradient of depth sensitivity, with a data-driven binary partition as the strongest structure: $k{=}2$ clustering in standardized $(|\rho|, d)$ space yields silhouette\,=\,0.632 (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-validation}), separating \emph{drifting} features (entropy mean, TTR, hapax ratio; $|\rho| > 0.60$, $d{=}0.76$--$1.17$) from \emph{non-drifting} ones.
We use the shorthand \emph{differential depth response} (DDR) for this partition and further resolve a 3/1/3 characterization using domain-informed criteria: entropy std occupies a sole \emph{intermediate} position (large level shift $d{=}0.55$, low monotonicity $|\rho|{=}0.16$); the remaining three \emph{near-stationary} features (entropy max, tail decay, entropy min) show negligible depth effects ($d < 0.10$; CV shift $<$3\% vs.\ $>$15\% for drifting).
This partition is robust under heteroscedasticity-corrected metrics (below).
The partition is demonstrated for this seven-feature set; alternative features (e.g., syntactic complexity, n-gram frequencies) may yield different groupings, though the convergence of five independent effect-size metrics suggests the location/shape asymmetry reflects distributional structure rather than feature-selection artifact.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{fig1_differential_response.pdf}
\caption{Differential depth response: Spearman correlations between individual features and generation depth. Drifting features (hapax ratio, TTR, entropy mean) show $|\rho| > 0.60$; entropy std ($|\rho|{=}0.16$, $d{=}0.55$) is the sole intermediate feature; near-stationary features (entropy max, tail decay, entropy min) show $d < 0.10$ for gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+ (entropy min's elevated pooled $|\rho|$ reflects the gen-0/gen-1 boundary; \S\ref{sec:results-differential}).}
\label{fig:feature-drift}
\end{figure}

Pooled class-balanced Spearman correlations with depth confirm the split (Figure~\ref{fig:feature-drift}):
drifting features show substantial monotonic trends (hapax ratio $\rho = -0.64$, TTR $\rho = -0.63$, entropy mean $\rho = -0.60$),
while shape features remain near-stationary (tail decay $|\rho| = 0.04$; per-depth distributions in Appendix~\ref{app:feature-distributions}).
The six-fold magnitude gap between drifting ($|\rho| > 0.60$) and near-stationary features ($|\rho| < 0.10$) defines the DDR partition, with entropy std ($|\rho| = 0.16$, $d{=}0.55$) as the sole intermediate member.
The 3/1/3 partition is stable across $d$ thresholds in $[0.56, 0.75]$; data-driven clustering confirms the primary drifting/non-drifting split ($k{=}2$, silhouette\,=\,0.632; Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-validation}).

\paragraph{Distributional shift quantification.}
Two-sample KS tests confirm the split: drifting-feature statistics (0.516--0.537) are ${\sim}10\times$ larger than shape-feature statistics (0.043--0.052; all $p \approx 0$ after Bonferroni correction).
Cohen's $d$ \cite{cohen1988statistical} (pooled, class-balanced) converges with $\rho$: drifting features show large effects (entropy mean $d{=}1.17$, TTR $d{=}0.88$, hapax ratio $d{=}0.76$), while shape features are near zero (entropy max $d{=}0.08$, tail decay $d{=}0.08$).
Levene tests reject strict equal-variance ($p < 10^{-10}$); Glass's $\Delta$ (using gen-1 SD) amplifies drifting effects (entropy mean $\Delta{=}1.41$, hapax $\Delta{=}0.94$) while near-stationary features remain negligible ($\Delta \leq 0.10$), yielding a ${\geq}9.5\times$ gap. Cliff's $\delta$ corroborates the partition (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-validation}).
Shape-feature CV shift ($<$3\% vs.\ $>$15\% for drifting features) supports ``near-stationary'' as a practical characterization.
Five features fall cleanly into the drifting or near-stationary groups under both $\rho$ and $d$; the remaining two require qualification: entropy min's pooled $|\rho|$ (0.40) reflects change concentrated at the gen-0/gen-1 boundary, but for gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+ it is near-stationary ($d{=}0.03$), placing it in the near-stationary group; entropy std shows a substantial level shift ($d{=}0.55$) despite low monotonicity ($|\rho|{=}0.16$), making it the sole intermediate feature.
Entropy min exhibits a discrepancy between location-based (Cohen's $d$\,=\,0.016) and rank-based (Cliff's $\delta$\,=\,0.354) effect sizes, indicating distributional shape change without location shift: recursive generation produces more extreme minimum-entropy tokens while preserving the mean. The near-stationary label refers specifically to location stability; rank-order sensitivity is documented in Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-validation}.
The location/shape decomposition rests on the convergence of $\rho$, Levene, CV shift, and $d$, not the omnibus KS statistic alone.
Per-generator TOST equivalence testing confirms the partition is not a pooling artifact; holdout generator validation confirms stability across two 4/4 splits (Appendix~\ref{app:tost}).
Tail decay shows generator-dependent variation ($d{=}0.15$--$0.22$), but reclassifying it as intermediate preserves the core split and classification performance.

\paragraph{Feature complementarity.}
The full 7-feature set (F1\,=\,0.773) outperforms surface-only (0.688) and reference-only (0.713; McNemar $p \approx 0$; Appendix~\ref{app:ablation-table}).
Permutation importance: hapax ratio (0.35), entropy mean (0.23), TTR (0.18).
PCA confirms the three drifting features share a single latent dimension (92.3\% variance, loadings 0.56--0.59; Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-feature-correlation}); replacing them with PC1 costs only 1.1\,pp binary F1, and retaining any single drifting feature with the four non-drifting features yields F1\,=\,0.692 (vs.\ 0.701 full).
DDR's contribution is identifying which distributional properties (NLL location vs.\ shape) are depth-sensitive; PC scores achieve equivalent classification but obscure which specific properties drift.
TTR and hapax ratio ($r = 0.97$) show permutation importance differences (0.35 vs.\ 0.18) due to feature masking \cite{strobl_conditional_2008}; all three are retained for marginal LOFO gains (Appendix~\ref{app:lofo}).

\paragraph{Cross-family reference models.}
Alternative references (OLMo-2-1B, Qwen3-0.6B) achieve comparable LOGO F1 (spread 0.013; Table~\ref{tab:cross-ref} in Appendix~\ref{app:cross-ref}), with consistently negative entropy drift.
Pythia generators' highest F1 (0.718--0.724) may partly reflect same-family affinity with the Pythia-410M reference model, but the 0.013 cross-reference spread bounds this effect; depth features are robust to reference model choice, though this does not alone establish DDR as a fundamental property of recursive generation.

\paragraph{Temperature and prompt-type sensitivity.}
The depth signal is modulated by decoding parameters and prompt type (Appendices~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity},~\ref{app:prompt-type}).
All four tested generators degrade at $t{=}0.9$ ($-9.3$ to $-26.0$\,pp binary F1); low-temperature improvement is model-family-dependent ($+7$--$9$\,pp for Pythia/OLMo at $t{=}0.5$, negligible for Qwen).
Continuation chains show the strongest drift (binary F1\,=\,0.781), with cross-prompt-type transfer confirming shared signal (LOPTO F1\,=\,0.753).
Per-feature convergence trajectories confirm this ordering (Appendix~\ref{app:convergence}); the DDR partition hierarchy is preserved across temperatures despite absolute effect-size compression (Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-temp-stability}).


\subsection{Comparison with Detection Baselines}
\label{sec:results-baselines}

Do existing detection methods already capture depth signal?
To contextualize depth discrimination ability rather than claim competitive advantage, we repurpose four detection scores as ordinal depth predictors using the same XGBoost framework and LOGO splits (Table~\ref{tab:baselines}).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Method} & \textbf{Feat.} & \textbf{3-cl F1} & \textbf{Bin F1} & \textbf{ms/text} \\
\midrule
4-det.\ + surface     & 6 & \textbf{0.795} & \textbf{0.708} & 22.8 \\
4-detector ens.\      & 4 & 0.785 & 0.700 & 22.8 \\
7-feature (ours)      & 7 & 0.774 & 0.705 & \textbf{9.7} \\
Avg-LogProb           & 1 & 0.707 & 0.673 & N/A \\
FastDetectGPT         & 1 & 0.660 & 0.569 & N/A \\
LD-Score              & 1 & 0.630 & 0.675 & N/A \\
Binoculars            & 1 & 0.411 & 0.539 & N/A \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Depth classification (8-gen LOGO, pooled evaluation; slightly higher than per-generator macro average in Table~\ref{tab:logo-results}). Identical XGBoost configuration. 7-feature: one 410M model (905\,MB); 4-det ensembles: two models, 1.4B params (2{,}868\,MB). Individual detection scores (N/A) share the reference-model forward pass; per-method timing is not separately profiled.}
\label{tab:baselines}
\end{table}

The 7-feature ensemble exceeds all individual baselines in 3-class F1 ($\Delta$\,=\,6.7--36.3\,pp).
Multi-detector ensembles achieve marginally higher binary F1 (0.708 vs.\ 0.705) at 2.4$\times$ inference cost, suggesting depth information is implicitly encoded in distributional divergence measures.
DDR's contribution is not classification performance but decomposing depth signal into location-sensitive and shape-stable components, a distinction absent from both binary detection methods and model collapse analyses (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The central finding is that recursive generation alters \emph{where} the token-level surprise distribution sits but not \emph{how} it is shaped: autoregressive sampling with fixed top-$p$ plausibly truncates the conditional distribution at a consistent shape regardless of input, while mean surprisal systematically decreases as the model conditions on its own increasingly typical outputs.
This asymmetry is not intrinsic to recursion but parameter-dependent: at $t{=}1.0$, the location signal collapses ($\rho$ from $-0.60$ to $-0.002$; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}), and semantic-preservation constraints attenuate drift (elaboration F1\,=\,0.730 vs.\ continuation 0.781; Appendix~\ref{app:prompt-type}), consistent with \citet{broken_telephone}; cross-type transfer remains viable (F1\,=\,0.753).

Several boundary conditions constrain practical applicability.
Document-level gen-1 per-class F1\,=\,0.63 is insufficient for automated filtering but sufficient for corpus-level flagging ($O(1/\sqrt{n})$ error scaling); the primary difficulty is distinguishing gen-1 from gen-2+, consistent with DDR producing the smallest location shift at the first recursive step (86\% false negatives; Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}).
Cross-temperature transfer degrades when test-time temperature exceeds training ($t{=}0.7 \rightarrow 1.0$: overall F1 from 0.789 to 0.723, with the most affected generator dropping to 0.418; Appendix~\ref{app:cross-temp}); depth fingerprinting assumes matched or lower temperature.
These patterns hold across reference model families (F1 within 0.013; Table~\ref{tab:cross-ref}).

DDR occupies a distinct position among recursive generation phenomena.
Model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse} describes irreversible degradation from \emph{retraining} on model outputs; inference-chain drift operates in a different regime where parameters are fixed, drift is fully reversible, and shape features are affected an order of magnitude less.
This divergence has practical implications: model collapse remediation focuses on restoring tail coverage, while inference-chain contamination preserves shape and thus requires location-based detection---a strategy that DDR directly enables.
Three depth classes represent the practical resolution ceiling (5-class F1\,$\approx$\,0.50; Appendix~\ref{app:finer-depth}), though richer representations recover substantially more signal (QLoRA F1\,=\,0.905; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}).
Instruction-tuned models show attenuated fingerprints (OLMo-Instruct LOGO F1\,=\,0.338 vs.\ 0.763 base), but QLoRA on instruct data (F1\,=\,0.89--0.91 vs.\ XGBoost 0.58--0.73; Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}) indicates instruction tuning reorganizes rather than eliminates the signal, though this is demonstrated under within-model CV only; cross-generator instruct transfer (XGBoost LOGO F1\,=\,0.487) remains weak.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

When the output of a language model is fed back as input to another (or the same) model, the resulting generation chain defines a discrete dynamical system over text distributions.
How do the distributional properties of generated text evolve across successive steps of this recursion?
Understanding this evolution is fundamental to characterizing how language models transform distributions under iterative conditioning, with implications for model collapse theory \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse} and data provenance \cite{ccnet,dsir} as model outputs increasingly re-enter training corpora \cite{dolma,fineweb} (an estimated 7--17\% of recent scientific publications contain substantial LLM-modified content \cite{mapping_llm_science,monitoring_ai_review}).
Yet existing detection methods \cite{fast_detectgpt,binoculars,ld_score,detectgpt} provide only binary real-vs-synthetic decisions, conflating qualitatively different material: a first-generation continuation retains much of the source distribution's lexical properties, while deeper recursive text exhibits measurably reduced vocabulary diversity and compressed perplexity.

We formulate \emph{generation depth classification}, classifying text by coarse ordinal depth (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+) rather than a binary label, and refer to the overall framework as \emph{depth fingerprinting}.
Concurrent studies characterize convergence in paraphrastic and translation chains \cite{broken_telephone,markovian_chains}, but none decompose the drift into structurally distinct components; our work addresses this gap in non-paraphrastic continuation chains.
We restrict to base (pretrained) models as a deliberate design choice: instruction-tuning introduces confounds (length regulation, format constraints, safety-driven shaping) that obscure the distributional dynamics of recursive generation; preliminary experiments confirm substantially degraded depth signal under instruction tuning (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

The key finding is a \emph{differential depth response} (DDR): when we measure how eight base-model generators from five families (Pythia, OLMo, Qwen, Llama, Mistral; 0.6B--8B parameters) transform text across recursive depths, central-tendency and diversity features (reference-model mean entropy, type-token ratio, hapax ratio) drift monotonically, while shape features (entropy max, tail decay) show an order-of-magnitude smaller effect size.
This pattern is consistent with recursive generation producing a location shift in the token-level NLL distribution; one hypothesis is that the softmax architecture and fixed sampling parameters constrain distributional shape under standard decoding regimes, while each successive generation compresses the location toward the model's preferred output distribution.

Because drifting features capture the progressive location shift while stationary features provide a stable reference, combining them yields a classifier that generalizes across generators: binary F1\,=\,0.764 on heterogeneous cross-model chains and 0.694 under leave-one-generator-out evaluation, outperforming individual detection baselines by 6.7--36.3\,pp while matching a 4-detector ensemble (within 0.3\,pp) at 2.4$\times$ lower computational cost.

Our contributions are threefold:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item We formulate generation depth classification, moving beyond binary detection to ordinal depth estimation (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+), and construct an evaluation suite of 37K texts from eight generators spanning five model families (0.6B--8B parameters).
    \item We decompose inference-chain drift into structurally distinct components: central-tendency features drift monotonically ($d = 0.76$--$1.17$) while shape features remain an order of magnitude more stable ($d < 0.10$), a decomposition absent from existing attractor dynamics and model collapse analyses. A 7-feature ensemble exploiting this \emph{differential depth response} achieves binary F1\,=\,0.764 on cross-model chains.
    \item Comprehensive evaluation reveals that DDR is robust within $t \in [0.5, 0.7]$ but degrades at $t{=}0.9$ ($-9.3$ to $-26.0$\,pp), is prompt-type modulated (continuation $>$ elaboration), and is absent in instruction-tuned models; equivalence testing (TOST $\pm$2\%, $p < 0.001$) confirms no downstream quality degradation (Appendix~\ref{app:downstream}).
\end{enumerate}

% Abstract — Depth Fingerprinting of Recursive LLM Generation Chains
\begin{abstract}
Recursive LLM generation shifts \emph{where} text sits in distributional space but leaves \emph{how} it is shaped nearly unchanged, and this asymmetry is consistent across five model families spanning 0.6B to 8B parameters.
We term this \emph{differential depth response} (DDR): under standard decoding, mean entropy and lexical diversity drift monotonically with generation depth while entropy max and tail decay show an order-of-magnitude smaller effect size.
Prior work on iterative generation tracks aggregate convergence without separating what changes from what is preserved; DDR provides this decomposition and enables coarse depth classification (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+): a 7-feature ensemble achieves leak-free binary F1\,=\,0.694 (95\% CI [.688, .700]) under leave-one-generator-out evaluation and 0.764 on cross-model chains, at lower cost than multi-detector alternatives.
Despite measurable distributional drift, equivalence testing (TOST $\pm$2\%, $p < 0.001$) confirms no downstream training quality degradation.
The depth signal degrades under instruction tuning; current applicability is restricted to base models.
\end{abstract}

[Reviewer 回复]:
[severity: info] **任务 A：R28 审稿 GPU 预判 — 5 个攻击面逐项评估**

---

### 攻击面 1：Base-Only Scope（"只测 base 模型，instruct 才是真实场景"）

**概率：高（~80%）** — 这是最显眼的攻击面。任何审稿人都会问。

**可能要求的 GPU 实验：**
- 扩展 instruct 实验到 5+ 模型（当前仅 3 个），跑完整 LOGO
- 模型：OLMo-2-1B-Inst, Qwen3-1.7B-Inst, Qwen3-0.6B-Inst + 至少 Llama-3.2-3B-Inst, Mistral-7B-Inst-v0.3
- 流程：数据生成（~3h/model × 2 = 6h）+ 特征提取（~1h）+ LOGO + QLoRA（~4h）
- 总计：~11h GPU，4 卡并行 ~3h wall clock

**DDL 前可完成？** YES（轻松）

**建议：等审稿结果再跑。** 理由：
1. 论文已有 3-gen instruct 实验 + QLoRA 恢复 + "reorganizes rather than eliminates" 叙事 + Limitations 诚实标注
2. Abstract L7 + Conclusion L6 已明确 scope = base models
3. 预跑风险：5-gen instruct LOGO 可能更差（当前 3-gen 已是 0.487），负面结果需要重新调整 narrative
4. **如果审稿人真要求**：DDL 后有 6 周 rebuttal 期，4 卡 11h = 半天搞定

---

### 攻击面 2：Feature Dependence（"7 个手工特征为什么够？"）

**概率：中（~40%）** — QLoRA (F1=0.905) 已部分回答

**可能要求的 GPU 实验：**
- BERT/RoBERTa 作为特征提取器（学习表示 vs 手工特征）
- ~8h GPU（fine-tune + LOGO evaluation）

**DDL 前可完成？** YES

**建议：不预跑。** 理由：
1. QLoRA 已证明"更丰富表示可提取更多信号"（+11.6pp）
2. Method L35 + L61 明确解释：选手工特征是为了 DDR 可解释性，不是为分类性能
3. Results L130: "DDR's contribution is not classification performance but decomposing depth signal"
4. 这个攻击的正确回应是文本澄清，不是实验

---

### 攻击面 3：Marginal Gain（"F1=0.694 太低，ensemble 还 0.708"）

**概率：中高（~55%）** — 但这是 text-defense 攻击，不是 experiment 攻击

**可能要求的 GPU 实验：**
- 更强的 feature engineering / AutoML
- ~10-20h（feature search + evaluation）

**DDL 前可完成？** 勉强

**建议：不预跑。** 理由：
1. 论文定位是 **task formulation + DDR decomposition**，不是 SOTA 分类器
2. Results L129-130 已预防："DDR's contribution is not classification performance but decomposing depth signal into location-sensitive and shape-stable components"
3. 提升 F1 不改变 DDR 发现的科学价值
4. **最可能的审稿人 action**: 要求更好的 framing/hedging（文本修复），而非新实验

---

### 攻击面 4：DDR 因果性（"相关≠因果，DDR 可能是 artifact"）

**概率：低中（~25%）** — 论文已有 5 个 convergent metrics

**可能要求的 GPU 实验：**
- 因果干预实验（controlled generation with modified attention/sampling）
- ~20-40h GPU（需要修改模型推理代码 + 生成 + 分析）

**DDL 前可完成？** 非常紧张，且代码量大

**建议：不预跑。** 理由：
1. 论文用 5 个独立 effect-size metrics（ρ, d, KS, Glass's Δ, Cliff's δ）convergence 作为 evidence
2. Results L80: "rests on the convergence of ρ, Levene, CV shift, and d, not the omnibus KS statistic alone"
3. 因果干预实验超出本文 scope（observational study → mechanistic 是 follow-up）
4. Intro L14 已用 "one hypothesis is that" 恰当 hedging

---

### 攻击面 5：Scale Limitation（"只到 8B，frontier 怎样？"）

**概率：中（~45%）** — Limitations L12-13 已标注

**可能要求的 GPU 实验：**
- 13B-70B 模型（量化后可跑在 32GB 卡上）
- Llama-3.1-70B-Q4 或 Qwen2.5-72B-Q4
- ~20-30h GPU（量化推理慢 + 1000 chains × 5 depths）

**DDL 前可完成？** 紧张但理论上可行（4 卡 ~8h wall clock）

**建议：不预跑。** 理由：
1. Limitations L13: "the consistent scale trend (Mistral-7B binary F1=0.633, lowest) suggests depth signal may weaken further at frontier scales" — 已诚实预测
2. 量化引入额外变量（quantization error vs depth signal），需要额外 ablation 验证
3. 负面结果概率高（基于 scale trend 外推），且需要复杂解释
4. 如果审稿人要求，rebuttal 期 4 卡足够

---

### 额外攻击面（从精读中发现）

**攻击面 6：TOST 3-seed 问题**
- 概率：低（~20%）— 论文已说 "preliminary observation"
- 如要求：多跑 7-10 个 seed 的 downstream fine-tuning，~10h GPU
- 建议：不预跑。负面结果本身就是论文结论之一。

**攻击面 7：Cross-domain t=1.0 confound**
- 概率：低（~15%）— appendix_domain 已有 t=0.7 补充数据 + 详细解释
- 建议：不预跑。

---

## 总结

| 攻击面 | R28 概率 | 需 GPU？ | 预跑？ | 理由 |
|--------|----------|----------|--------|------|
| Base-only | 高 80% | 11h | ❌ 等 | 已有 3-gen + QLoRA + honest scope |
| Feature dep. | 中 40% | 8h | ❌ 等 | QLoRA 已回答 + 文本 defense |
| Marginal gain | 中高 55% | 10-20h | ❌ 等 | 定位是 DDR 不是 SOTA |
| DDR causality | 低中 25% | 20-40h | ❌ 等 | 5 metrics convergence + hedging |
| Scale | 中 45% | 20-30h | ❌ 等 | 量化引入 confound + 已 hedge |
| TOST seeds | 低 20% | 10h | ❌ 等 | 已标注 preliminary |
| Domain confound | 低 15% | 5h | ❌ 等 | 已有 t=0.7 补充 |

**结论：全部 7 个维度均为"等审稿结果再跑"。**

核心逻辑：
1. 所有攻击面的**文本防御**已就位（hedging + scope qualification + honest limitations）
2. 预跑实验的**负面结果风险 > 正面收益**（特别是 instruct 和 scale）
3. R28 结果到手后有 **6 周 rebuttal 期**，4× RTX 5090 可在 24h 内完成任何单项补实验
4. GPU 空闲的机会成本为零（无其他项目竞争）
5. **最高 ROI 仍然是 5 个文本修复**（Discussion L10/L9, Conclusion L6, Results L57/L129）

\section*{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

All eight generators are base (pretrained) models.
This is a deliberate design choice: base models isolate the generation mechanism from instruction-tuning effects, enabling controlled study of recursive distributional drift.
However, web text is predominantly produced by instruction-tuned and RLHF-aligned models.
Preliminary instruct experiments confirm that depth signal degrades substantially under instruction tuning: OLMo-2-1B-Instruct drops to LOGO F1\,=\,0.338 (vs.\ 0.763 base) and Qwen3-0.6B with chat template to 0.667 (vs.\ 0.816 under a 7-generator split).
Length-matched analysis yields near-zero correlations ($|\rho| < 0.02$) and binary classification near chance (F1\,$\approx$\,0.5) for Qwen models, leaving interpretation ambiguous.
Extending depth fingerprinting to instruct models requires addressing these confounds (length regulation, format constraints, safety-driven distribution shaping) that instruction tuning introduces.

Our experiments include generators up to 8.2B parameters (Qwen3-8B).
Depth signal persists at this scale (Qwen3-8B 3-class F1\,=\,0.714), but cross-scale transfer incurs a moderate gap vs.\ $\leq$2.8B generators (F1\,=\,0.77--0.81).
Frontier models (70B+) remain untested; their higher fluency may further compress feature margins.

Differential depth response strength is prompt-type dependent: continuation chains show strongest drift (within-type F1\,=\,0.781) compared to elaboration (0.730), rewriting (0.737), and paraphrastic chains (binary F1\,=\,0.671 vs.\ 0.749 for continuation).
DDR is most reliably detected in continuation-style generation; near-paraphrastic settings approach the method's detection floor.
Cross-prompt-type transfer (LOPTO F1\,=\,0.753) confirms shared signal, yet additional prompt types (e.g., summarization, instruction following) and cross-generator $\times$ cross-prompt interactions remain untested.

Our primary evaluation uses single-generator chains; cross-model chains (\S\ref{sec:results-classification}) confirm depth signal under generator heterogeneity (3-class F1\,=\,0.809, binary F1\,=\,0.764), though the eight generators represent a controlled laboratory setting rather than the full diversity of real-world contamination.
Simulated human editing (\S\ref{sec:discussion}) suggests graceful degradation, but the gap between simulated token replacement and real-world post-processing remains untested.
Independent gen-0 seed sets per generator would eliminate potential memorization effects in 3-class LOGO evaluation; we report leak-free binary F1 as the primary metric to mitigate this limitation.

The reference model is fixed to Pythia-410M throughout, although cross-family reference experiments (\S\ref{sec:results-differential}) confirm the phenomenon is not reference-specific (spread 0.013 across three references).
All seed texts in the main evaluation are English Wikipedia excerpts.
Cross-domain evaluation (Appendix~\ref{app:domain}) shows that depth signal persists across News, Academic, and Code domains (binary F1 $>$ 0.73 under LOGO at $t{=}1.0$), though a domain $\times$ temperature interaction exists: certain domain/generator combinations at lower temperature approach chance level (e.g., Academic domain binary F1\,=\,0.628 at $t{=}0.7$), suggesting that reference model calibration is critical for cross-domain deployment.
The reference model dependency (Pythia-410M, English-centric pretraining) limits non-English applicability and adds inference overhead relative to surface-feature-only approaches.
Generalization to other languages remains untested.

Our default analysis uses fixed decoding parameters (temperature 0.7, nucleus $p{=}0.9$). A sampling ablation (Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}) shows robustness to moderate variation ($t \in [0.5, 0.7]$, ${\leq}0.3$\,pp) but substantial degradation at $t{=}1.0$ ($-6$\,pp), indicating that depth fingerprinting assumes standard decoding regimes.
Cross-temperature transfer shows substantial degradation when test-time temperature exceeds training-time settings, limiting deployment to scenarios where the generation temperature is approximately known.

We use 3-class granularity (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+). A 5-class evaluation (Appendix~\ref{app:finer-depth}) yields LOGO F1\,$\approx$\,0.50, with depths 2--4 mutually indistinguishable, validating the 3-class design as the practical resolution limit.

% Abstract — Depth Fingerprinting of Recursive LLM Generation Chains
\begin{abstract}
Recursive LLM generation shifts \emph{where} text sits in distributional space but leaves \emph{how} it is shaped nearly unchanged, and this asymmetry is consistent across five model families spanning 0.6B to 8B parameters.
We term this \emph{differential depth response} (DDR): under standard decoding, mean entropy and lexical diversity drift monotonically with generation depth while entropy max and tail decay show an order-of-magnitude smaller effect size.
Prior work on iterative generation tracks aggregate convergence without separating what changes from what is preserved; DDR provides this decomposition and enables coarse depth classification (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+): a 7-feature ensemble achieves leak-free binary F1\,=\,0.694 (95\% CI [.688, .700]) under leave-one-generator-out evaluation and 0.764 on cross-model chains, at lower cost than multi-detector alternatives.
Despite measurable distributional drift, equivalence testing (TOST $\pm$2\%, $p < 0.001$) confirms no downstream training quality degradation.
The depth signal degrades under instruction tuning; current applicability is restricted to base models.
\end{abstract}

1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	Recursive generation produces a consistent, interpretable distributional signature: central-tendency features drift monotonically across depth while shape features remain an order of magnitude more stable.
5	This differential depth response enables depth classification across five model families (leak-free binary F1\,=\,0.694 under LOGO evaluation, 0.764 on cross-model chains) with no downstream quality degradation (TOST $\pm$2\%, $p < 0.001$).
6	The location-shape decomposition suggests that depth signal may arise in any iterative autoregressive process with fixed decoding, a hypothesis testable beyond text generation; current boundaries remain at instruction tuning (where token-level signal persists but handcrafted features fail to capture it) and frontier scale (70B+).
7	Code, data, and models will be released upon publication.

21	    \item We decompose inference-chain drift into structurally distinct components: central-tendency features drift monotonically ($d = 0.76$--$1.17$) while shape features remain an order of magnitude more stable ($d < 0.10$), a decomposition absent from existing attractor dynamics and model collapse analyses. A 7-feature ensemble exploiting this \emph{differential depth response} achieves binary F1\,=\,0.764 on cross-model chains.

23	\end{enumerate}
